title: His Master Taken from His Head
description: His Master Taken from His Head in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 73, “On the death of a minister”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: His mas-ter ta-ken from his head, El-i-sha saw him go; And, in de-spond-ing ac-cents said, "Ah, what must Is-rael do!"

lines: His master taken from his head,
But he forgot the Lord, who lifts
Nor knew, that all Elijah's gifts
Would soon be made his own.
What! when a Paul has run his course,
Yes, while the dear Redeemer lives,
And shall be fed with what he gives,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
